A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLCF study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original checklist evaluations, language-model training results, reward comparisons, ablations, and the response-pair filtering experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of non-target capabilities and off-policy training of Llama and OLMo.

M1.justification: The extraction, judging, filtering, and DPO pipeline is retained. However, Section 2 changes from one universal item containing two criteria, weighted 100, to two requirements with total weight 100. The unchanged appendix prompts do not establish whether separate scoring was introduced or this is only a wording change.

E1.justification: v2 adds XSTest, GSM8K, and TruthfulQA, extending downstream evaluation to appropriate refusal, mathematical reasoning, and truthfulness. These test capabilities beyond the original instruction-following benchmarks and reward-ranking evaluation. WildChat training coverage and the earlier benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain SFT, Skywork, ArmoRM, UltraFeedback, and the prompted AI Judge. The new non-target evaluations reuse Skywork; the Llama and OLMo experiments compare RLCF with their starting models. No new competing alignment algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.6 introduces an off-policy experimental design: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and OLMo 2 7B Instruct train on Qwen-generated, Qwen-scored preference pairs. Table 9 additionally introduces XSTest safe/unsafe/overall scores, GSM8K accuracy, and TruthfulQA MC1/MC2 evaluation. The original Qwen training budgets and settings remain.

E4.justification: New Sections 5.5–5.6 test whether instruction-following gains sacrifice underrepresented capabilities and whether checklist supervision transfers across model families. Table 8 removes the dyspraxia case study. Earlier checklist-generation and scoring ablations, judge-sample sensitivity, and Appendix A's filtering analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the qualitative IFEval variance caveat and the existing analysis of averaging 3, 5, 10, or 25 judge samples; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, but Tables 9–10 add substantial evidence. Newly reported comparisons include Qwen GSM8K accuracy of 83.2 before RLCF versus 82.2 afterward, and Llama FollowBench HSR of 68.0 versus 72.3 with off-policy RLCF. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1's reported scores. Table 8 removes the dyspraxia results and edits retained response examples without changing their scores.

T1.justification: The checklist definition and conceptual requirements are retained. Neither version contains a theoretical development, theorem, proof, or formal derivation that is added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim that Qwen-generated preference data can improve Llama and OLMo off-policy. The central contributions—candidate-based checklist generation, WildChecklists, checklist scoring, and improved instruction following—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's RewardBench safety caveat, v2 explains trade-offs in unsafe-prompt refusal, mathematics, and truthfulness, links them to WildChat's domain imbalance, and proposes broader prompt coverage. It also interprets cross-family transfer as evidence of reusable criteria. These substantially expand the applicability discussion, although the conclusion still claims uniform improvement across all considered benchmarks.

D1.justification: v2 announces a public release and supplies code and dataset locations, replacing v1's future-release promise. Most training details and both appendix prompts remain. However, v2 omits the explicit judge temperature, reward-baseline scalar-gap filtering rule, and Boolean-to-0/100 conversion description. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish changed execution.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds substantive comparisons with contemporaneous Wang et al. (2025b) and Dineen et al. (2025), qualifying the priority claim and distinguishing instruction-specific rubrics from global criteria and GRPO. References also add the new benchmark/model sources and remove Meng et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 tightens paragraphs across the introduction, method, results, and limitations, increasingly uses 'rubrics' for checklists, and reorders related-work paragraphs. It inserts two results subsections and updates the venue text and acknowledgements, while preserving the overall section sequence and narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–10, reduces Table 8 from three cases to two, revises some captions, and relocates existing tables and Figure 3. Existing figures and the visual template are retained. Appendix B–C headings move onto a mostly empty separate page, while their prompt figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Tables 9–10 strengthen v1's Qwen-only study with cross-family transfer evidence and explicit tests revealing non-target capability losses. This improves understanding of applicability and limitations, while the new resource locations aid reproducibility. The gains are tempered by the conclusion's retained uniform-improvement claim, which is overbroad given Table 9, and the removal of some implementation details.
